主要内容: The U.S. Department of the Treasury introduced a new methodology for estimating holdings of Treasury securities, effective with the February 29, 2012 release. This update incorporates new data from the TIC Form SLT, which reports long-term Treasury securities held by foreign investors. The SLT data, collected in September and December 2011, includes holdings of long-term securities (original maturity of more than one year), such as Treasury securities. Short-term Treasury holdings are reported on TIC Form BL-2, which includes data on short-term liabilities to foreigners. Starting in January 2012, SLT data will be collected monthly, with the MFH table updated on a rolling basis. The new methodology also integrates net transactions data to estimate holdings for the most recent month. Revised data for October and November 2011 reflect this new approach, combining SLT data with net purchases. Data for earlier months through August 2011 are based on the previous methodology. Periodic surveys, conducted annually since June 2002, provide the starting position for long-term Treasury holdings, with the most recent survey as of June 2011. Estimates between surveys are constructed by adding monthly net purchases to the latest survey data. The U.S. Department of the Treasury provides estimates of holdings of Treasury securities, which are influenced by custodial and transaction biases. For example, a German investor holding U.S. securities through a Swiss bank is recorded under Switzerland rather than Germany, contributing to the large recorded holdings in major custodial centers like Switzerland and Luxembourg. The methodology for estimating holdings has evolved to reduce distortions caused by transaction bias, which previously led to significant geographic discrepancies. The new methodology relies on transactions data for the most recent month, minimizing the impact of transaction bias over time. Holdings of short-term Treasury bills are reported at face value, while long-term securities are reported at market value. Data on short-term holdings is collected through the TIC form BL-2, and long-term holdings are estimated using periodic surveys and monthly net purchase data. The latest survey data for long-term holdings is as of June 2005, with earlier data available for previous years.
